data.description:
Michelle wants this eventually (2026-10-28): an organizer schedules the nights question from the host page while signed in, instead of `just schedule` with the admin token.

Source: Codex branch codex/app-question-scheduling, started 2026-10-11 on base 046779c (PR #67). One commit, ff574da "test: define organizer scheduling flow (RED)", plus uncommitted work across 26 files: GET /organizer/questions (approved, unused; id and topic only), POST /organizer/schedule (organizer auth, club-scoped, 409 on bad dates, unapproved ids and a question already held by a room), a host-page picker and date form, copy keys, and a SPEC.md "Organizer scheduling copy" section. The whole thing is saved as the attached patch.

Before building:
- Contract: D-20 says the laptop reaches the room through admin routes and one bearer token the client holds. This adds a second scheduling path that skips that token. Amend SPEC/BUILDPLAN first.
- The patch applies cleanly to 046779c but not to main: PQ-48 rekeyed scheduling by (club, question_id), and the room files have moved since. Port it rather than apply it.
- Untested: nobody has built the uncommitted half or run its tests.

QUESTION PQ-80 (amendment + design): SPEC §8.4 draft: "### 8.4 Choosing the question on the host phone (PQ-80) — A signed-in organizer can pick the night's question on the host phone instead of naming it in the host link. `GET /organizer/questions?club=‹club›` takes the organizer session and the same check as *Create a room*: the request names the club, and that club's role authorizes it (§8, AC-103). An unknown club is refused as a missing role is. It answers, with `Cache-Control: no-store`, with the questions scheduled for that club that the club can run today: affirmed, arranged for today's meetup date, not used by the club, and held by no room. Each is given as `id` and `topic` only. The organizer picks one and creates the room on it through `POST /rooms`, which applies the same checks again and refuses with the existing reasons if anything changed in between. The host phone schedules nothing: a question reaches the room only as §8.3 describes, arranged for the club's meetup date by `popquiz schedule` on the laptop, and the organizer may push several that way before the night. The record carries the date it was arranged for, and the room offers or creates on it only on that date. Listing and picking use nothing (G-10). The listing returns `id` and `topic` only; it adds no reader of the sealed module and arranges nothing. The room's existing projections and the reveal are unchanged. D-20 stands: the admin channel is still two routes and one token, and the organizer session does not open it." §11 keys: host_pick_legend: "Question", host_pick_choice: "‹id› · ‹topic›", host_pick_loading: "Loading questions…", host_pick_empty: "No question is ready for this club today.", host_pick_reload: "Reload", host_pick_load_failed: "Couldn't load the questions.", ROOM_QUESTION_OTHER_DATE (room reason, R1-a only): "That question was scheduled for another date." BUILDPLAN note (under D-E, after T-25): "2026-11-06 (PQ-80): the host phone lists the questions scheduled for the organizer's club and creates the room on the one picked (SPEC.md §8.4). This is not a third admin route or a second way in. The answer still enters only through PUT /admin/… with the admin token, and the listing takes the organizer session, which never opens /admin. The server may hold several scheduled questions per club; the organizer chooses among them on the night." Plus an M4 row T-27 (criteria AC-101, AC-103, AC-72, AC-92, AC-61; depends on T-07, T-10, T-25). New criterion: none recommended; AC-101 (answer only over the admin channel), AC-72/G-12 (affirmed only), AC-92/G-10 (used at release), AC-103 (club role), AC-61 (sealed module) cover it. Optional draft if you want one: AC-106 "A signed-in organizer can choose the night's question on the host phone from the questions scheduled for their club, shown by id and topic only. Choosing uses nothing, and the question still reaches the room only over the admin channel (AC-101)." Design: (1) source of questions: (b), your steer — laptop pushes over the admin channel, phone picks; plus the review's Major R1: the pushed record carries no date, so an unpicked shortlist would carry into the next meetup with the old date's answer slot. Recommend R1-a: `popquiz schedule` adds meetup_date to the PUT body, the room stores it as metadata and lists/creates only on that date (also closes the same hole on today's /host?question= path). Needs your clearance for a small hunk in pipeline/src/popquiz/schedule.py push + its test (PQ-58's area this wave) and server/admin.rs (400 on a body without the date). Alternative R1-b, no pipeline change: on release the room drops the club's other scheduled records; misses rooms that expire unreleased. (2) auth: the organizer bearer + authorize_create(bearer, club) exactly as POST /rooms; the club is named in the request and authorized by its role (deviation D1, session not club-bound); 401 no/expired session, 403 wrong_server, 403 wrong_role incl. unknown club, 503 Discord down; admin.rs check and admin_routes untouched; the new route is DRIVEN in canary_scan. (3) host page: radio fieldset "Question" (‹id› · ‹topic›, 44px rows, native checked mark, wraps, phone first) above the existing Create a room, disabled until chosen; Reload on empty/failed; 401 back to sign-in; a11y screens added. (4) state: no new store beyond the record's meetup date (R1-a); one read-only eligibility predicate shared by the listing and create_for, create stays authoritative under its lock order; listing returns {questions:[{id,topic}]} only, topic copied onto PublicQuestion at the existing split. (5) just schedule parity: there is one scheduling path (the admin PUT); test picker_lists_exactly_what_the_admin_channel_scheduled proves the pick and /host?question= create the same room with the same refusals. Plan review: FAIL (Codex), Majors: R1 shortlist not tied to its date; R2 incomplete auth matrix — both resolved in the plan, plus 4 Minors and 1 NIT accepted.
